title: Pharmacogenetic test (warfarin, clopidogrel)
what: This test shows how your genes affect the way some medicines work. It helps your doctor choose the medicine and the dose.
why: Before starting or when adjusting blood thinners and some other medicines, or if a medicine does not help or causes side effects.
duration: the sample usually takes 5 minutes; results usually come in a few days or 1 to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: All the medicines you take now
If a medicine caused strong side effects or bleeding
If you had a blood transfusion or a bone marrow transplant

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You usually do not need to fast. If a cheek swab is taken, do not eat, drink, or smoke for 30 minutes before.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop anything on your own. Medicines usually do not affect this test.

steps: The nurse takes blood from a vein into one tube
Sometimes a cotton swab is rubbed inside your cheek instead
If blood is taken, a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
The sample is labeled and sent to the lab
feel: A quick prick, or just a swab touching your cheek
The test is done once. It does not need to be repeated
after: Results usually come in a few days or 1 to 2 weeks
Take the result to your doctor. They will decide whether to change the medicine or the dose
Keep the report. It is useful for life
Do not change your doses on your own based on the result

faq.q: Does this test replace blood clotting tests?
faq.a: No. The gene test helps choose a starting dose, but you still need clotting checks.

faq.q: How many times do I need it?
faq.a: Once. Your genes do not change, so the result is good for life.

reminders.text: Pharmacogenetic test tomorrow. Bring a list of all the medicines you take.
